content.theory:
An **array** holds a fixed number of same-typed values. Two ways to create one:

```java
int[] scores = new int[4];           // array of 4 ints, all 0
String[] names = {"Ada", "Alan", "Linus"};  // with values
```

The **length is fixed** once created — you can't add items. `length` is a property (no parentheses):

```java
System.out.println(names.length);   // 3
```

Access and set by index — Java is 0-based:

```java
scores[0] = 95;
System.out.println(scores[0]);     // 95
System.out.println(names[1]);       // Alan
System.out.println(names[names.length - 1]);  // last item
```

Loop through with an index or the enhanced for-each:

```java
for (int i = 0; i < scores.length; i++) {
    System.out.println(scores[i]);
}

for (String name : names) {
    System.out.println(name);
}
```

Watch out: accessing `scores[10]` when the array has only 4 items throws an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

`ArrayList` (from `java.util`) is the growable alternative — but arrays are the foundation, so master them first.

exercise.instruction: Create a String[] 'colors' with values 'red', 'green', 'blue'. Print colors[0] and the array length.

quiz.question: What is the index of the last item in a 5-element array?
